task: r01t_fromager_distinfo_ticket
prompt: 'This is the fromager repository (Python wheel builder). A virtualenv with the project

  and test dependencies is already set up at `.venv`; run tests with

  `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts="" tests/...`.


  Fix the issue below. Add a regression test and run the relevant test file.


  Issue #1146: get_metadata_for_wheel() may return wrong metadata


  `get_metadata_for_wheel` returns the first match for `name.endswith(".dist-info/METADATA")`.

  This is a bad assumption. A wheel can contain multiple `.dist-info` directories. It''s

  common to include dist-info directories of vendored packages.


  `get_metadata_for_wheel` should only look at `dist-info` directories in the root of the

  wheel. Or better: parse the URL, split the name, and use

  `{dist_name}-{dist_version}.dist-info/METADATA`.

  '

import dataclasses
import datetime
import logging
import typing
from io import BytesIO
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit
from zipfile import ZipFile

from packaging.metadata import Metadata
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import BuildTag, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from .request_session import session

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclasses.dataclass
class Cooldown:
    """Policy for rejecting recently-published package versions.

    bootstrap_time is fixed at construction so all resolutions in a single run
    share the same cutoff.
    """

    min_age: datetime.timedelta
    bootstrap_time: datetime.datetime = dataclasses.field(
        default_factory=lambda: datetime.datetime.now(datetime.UTC)
    )


@dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True, order=True, slots=True, repr=False, kw_only=True)
class Candidate:
    name: str
    version: Version
    url: str
    is_sdist: bool | None = dataclasses.field(default=None)
    extras: tuple[str, ...] = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)
    build_tag: BuildTag = dataclasses.field(default=(), compare=False)
    has_metadata: bool = dataclasses.field(default=False, compare=False)
    remote_tag: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)
    remote_commit: str | None = dataclasses.field(default=None, compare=False)
    upload_time: datetime.datetime | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, compare=False
    )

    _metadata: Metadata | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, init=False, compare=False
    )
    _dependencies: list[Requirement] | None = dataclasses.field(
        default=None, init=False, compare=False
    )

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        # force normalized name
        object.__setattr__(self, "name", canonicalize_name(self.name))

    def __repr__(self) -> str:
        if not self.extras:
            return f"<{self.name}=={self.version}>"
        return f"<{self.name}[{','.join(self.extras)}]=={self.version}>"

    @property
    def metadata_url(self) -> str | None:
        """PEP 658: metadata is available at {url}.metadata"""
        if self.has_metadata:
            return self.url + ".metadata"
        return None

    @property
    def metadata(self) -> Metadata:
        if self._metadata is None:
            if not self.has_metadata:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.url} does not have metadata")
            metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(self.url, self.metadata_url)
            object.__setattr__(self, "_metadata", metadata)
        assert self._metadata
        return self._metadata

    def _get_dependencies(self) -> typing.Iterable[Requirement]:
        deps = self.metadata.requires_dist or []
        extras = self.extras if self.extras else [""]

        for r in deps:
            if r.marker is None:
                yield r
            else:
                for e in extras:
                    if r.marker.evaluate({"extra": e}):
                        yield r

    @property
    def dependencies(self) -> list[Requirement]:
        if self._dependencies is None:
            dependencies = list(self._get_dependencies())
            object.__setattr__(self, "_dependencies", dependencies)
        assert self._dependencies
        return self._dependencies

    @property
    def requires_python(self) -> str | None:
        spec = self.metadata.requires_python
        return str(spec) if spec is not None else None


def get_metadata_for_wheel(
    url: str, metadata_url: str | None = None, *, validate: bool = True
) -> Metadata:
    """Get metadata for a wheel, supporting PEP 658 metadata endpoints.

    Args:
        url: URL of the wheel file
        metadata_url: Optional URL of the metadata file (PEP 658)
        validate: Whether to validate metadata (default: True)

    Returns:
        Parsed metadata as a Metadata object
    """
    # Try PEP 658 metadata endpoint first if available
    if metadata_url:
        try:
            logger.debug(
                f"Attempting to fetch metadata from PEP 658 endpoint: {metadata_url}"
            )
            response = session.get(metadata_url)
            response.raise_for_status()

            # Parse metadata directly using packaging.metadata.Metadata
            # (avoiding circular import with dependencies module)
            metadata = Metadata.from_email(response.content, validate=validate)
            logger.debug(f"Successfully retrieved metadata via PEP 658 for {url}")
            return metadata

        except Exception as e:
            logger.debug(f"Failed to fetch PEP 658 metadata from {metadata_url}: {e}")
            logger.debug(
                "Falling back to downloading full wheel for metadata extraction"
            )

    # Fallback to existing method: download wheel and extract metadata.
    # The wheel may vendor other packages with their own .dist-info
    # directories, so look up the exact path derived from the wheel filename
    # (PEP 427: {name}-{version}-{tags}.whl).
    logger.debug(f"Downloading full wheel to extract metadata: {url}")
    filename = unquote(urlsplit(url).path.rsplit("/", 1)[-1])
    name, version = filename.split("-")[:2]
    metadata_path = f"{name}-{version}.dist-info/METADATA"
    data = session.get(url).content
    with ZipFile(BytesIO(data)) as z:
        if metadata_path in z.namelist():
            # Parse metadata directly using packaging.metadata.Metadata
            # (avoiding circular import with dependencies module)
            return Metadata.from_email(z.read(metadata_path), validate=validate)

    # If we didn't find the metadata, raise an error
    raise ValueError(f"Could not find {metadata_path} in wheel: {url}")

 """Tests for PEP 658 metadata support."""
 
 import typing
+from io import BytesIO
 from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
+from zipfile import ZipFile
 
+import pytest
 from packaging.version import Version
 
 from fromager.candidate import Candidate, get_metadata_for_wheel
 
 
+def _make_wheel(files: dict[str, bytes]) -> bytes:
+    """Build an in-memory wheel archive from a mapping of path to content."""
+    buf = BytesIO()
+    with ZipFile(buf, "w") as z:
+        for path, content in files.items():
+            z.writestr(path, content)
+    return buf.getvalue()
+
+
 class TestPEP658Support:
     """Test PEP 658 metadata support in fromager."""

get_metadata_for_wheel\n\n\nclass TestPEP658Support:\n    \"\"\"Test PEP 658 metadata support in fromager.\"\"\"\n\n    def test_candidate_with_metadata_url(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test that Candidate can be created with a metadata URL.\"\"\"\n        candidate = Candidate(\n            name=\"test-package\",\n            version=Version(\"1.0.0\"),\n            url=\"https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl\",\n            has_metadata=True,\n        )\n\n        assert (\n            candidate.metadata_url\n            == \"https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata\"\n        )\n\n    def test_candidate_without_metadata_url(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test that Candidate works without metadata URL (legacy behavior).\"\"\"\n        candidate = Candidate(\n            name=\"test-package\",\n            version=Version(\"1.0.0\"),\n            url=\"https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl\",\n        )\n\n        assert candidate.metadata_url is None\n\n    @patch(\"fromager.candidate.session\")\n    def test_get_metadata_with_pep658_success(self, mock_session: typing.Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test successful metadata retrieval via PEP 658 endpoint.\"\"\"\n        # Mock the metadata response\n        mock_response = Mock()\n        mock_response.content = b\"\"\"Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: test-package\nVersion: 1.0.0\nSummary: A test package\nRequires-Dist: requests >= 2.0.0\n\"\"\"\n        mock_response.raise_for_status.return_value = None\n        mock_session.get.return_value = mock_response\n\n        wheel_url = \"https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl\"\n        metadata_url = (\n            \"https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata\"\n        )\n\n        metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url)\n\n        # Verify the metadata was parsed correctly\n        assert metadata.name == \"test-package\"\n        assert str(metadata.version) == \"1.0.0\"\n        assert metadata.summary == \"A test package\"\n        assert metadata.requires_dist is not None\n        assert any(str(req) == \"requests>=2.0.0\" for req in metadata.requires_dist)\n\n        # Verify only the metadata URL was called, not the wheel URL\n        mock_session.get.assert_called_once_with(metadata_url)\n\n    @patch(\"fromager.candidate.session\")\n    def test_get_metadata_pep658_fallback_behavior(\n        self, mock_session: typing.Any\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test that PEP 658 is tried first, then falls back to wheel download.\"\"\"\n        # Mock that metadata URL fails, then wheel URL succeeds\n        responses = []\n\n        def side_effect(url: str) -> typing.Any:\n            if url.endswith(\".metadata\"):\n                # First call - metadata request fails\n                mock_response = Mock()\n                mock_response.raise_for_status.side_effect = Exception(\"404 Not Found\")\n                responses.append((\"metadata\", url))\n                return mock_response\n            else:\n                # Second call - wheel request\n                responses.append((\"wheel\", url))\n                raise Exception(\"Wheel parsing intentionally mocked to fail\")\n\n        mock_session.get.side_effect = side_effect\n\n        wheel_url = \"https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl\"\n        metadata_url = (\n            \"https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata\"\n        )\n\n        # This should raise an exception during wheel parsing, but we can verify the order\n        try:\n            get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url)\n        except Exception:\n            pass  # Expected to fail during wheel parsing mock\n\n        # Verify that both URLs were called in the correct order\n        assert len(responses) == 2\n        assert responses[0] == (\"metadata\", metadata_url)\n        assert responses[1] == (\"wheel\", wheel_url)\n        assert mock_session.get.call_count == 2\n\n    @patch(\"fromager.candidate.session\")\n    def test_get_metadata_without_pep658_behavior(\n        self, mock_session: typing.Any\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test that without PEP 658 metadata URL, only wheel URL is called.\"\"\"\n        # Mock wheel request\n        responses = []\n\n        def side_effect(url: str) -> typing.Any:\n            responses.append((\"wheel\", url))\n            raise Exception(\"Wheel parsing intentionally mocked to fail\")\n\n        mock_session.get.side_effect = side_effect\n\n        wheel_url = get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url=None)\n        except Exception:\n            pass  # Expected to fail during wheel parsing mock\n\n        # Verify that only the wheel URL was called\n        assert len(responses) == 1\n        assert responses[0] == (\"wheel\", wheel_url)\n        mock_session.get.assert_called_once_with(wheel_url)\n\n    def \"https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata\"\n        )\n\n    def test_candidate_without_metadata_url(self) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test that Candidate works without metadata url=\"https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl\",\n        )\n\n        assert candidate.metadata_url is None\n\n    @patch(\"fromager.candidate.session\")\n    def test_get_metadata_with_pep658_success(self, mock_session: typing.Any) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Test successful metadata retrieval via PEP 658 endpoint.\"\"\"\n        # Mock the metadata response\n        mock_response = Mock()\n        mock_response.content = b\"\"\"Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: test-package\nVersion: 1.0.0\nSummary: A test package\nRequires-Dist: requests >= 2.0.0\n\"\"\"\n        mock_response.raise_for_status.return_value = None\n        mock_session.get.return_value = mock_response\n\n        wheel_url = \"https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl\"\n        metadata_url = (\n            \"https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata\"\n        )\n\n        metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url)\n\n        # Verify """Tests for PEP 658 metadata support."""

import typing
from io import BytesIO
from unittest.mock import Mock, patch
from zipfile import ZipFile

import pytest
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager.candidate import Candidate, get_metadata_for_wheel


def _make_wheel(files: dict[str, bytes]) -> bytes:
    """Build an in-memory wheel archive from a mapping of path to content."""
    buf = BytesIO()
    with ZipFile(buf, "w") as z:
        for path, content in files.items():
            z.writestr(path, content)
    return buf.getvalue()


class TestPEP658Support:
    """Test PEP 658 metadata support in fromager."""

    def test_candidate_with_metadata_url(self) -> None:
        """Test that Candidate can be created with a metadata URL."""
        candidate = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            has_metadata=True,
        )

        assert (
            candidate.metadata_url
            == "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

    def test_candidate_without_metadata_url(self) -> None:
        """Test that Candidate works without metadata URL (legacy behavior)."""
        candidate = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
        )

        assert candidate.metadata_url is None

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_with_pep658_success(self, mock_session: typing.Any) -> None:
        """Test successful metadata retrieval via PEP 658 endpoint."""
        # Mock the metadata response
        mock_response = Mock()
        mock_response.content = b"""Metadata-Version: 2.1
Name: test-package
Version: 1.0.0
Summary: A test package
Requires-Dist: requests >= 2.0.0
"""
        mock_response.raise_for_status.return_value = None
        mock_session.get.return_value = mock_response

        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        metadata_url = (
            "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

        metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url)

        # Verify the metadata was parsed correctly
        assert metadata.name == "test-package"
        assert str(metadata.version) == "1.0.0"
        assert metadata.summary == "A test package"
        assert metadata.requires_dist is not None
        assert any(str(req) == "requests>=2.0.0" for req in metadata.requires_dist)

        # Verify only the metadata URL was called, not the wheel URL
        mock_session.get.assert_called_once_with(metadata_url)

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_pep658_fallback_behavior(
        self, mock_session: typing.Any
    ) -> None:
        """Test that PEP 658 is tried first, then falls back to wheel download."""
        # Mock that metadata URL fails, then wheel URL succeeds
        responses = []

        def side_effect(url: str) -> typing.Any:
            if url.endswith(".metadata"):
                # First call - metadata request fails
                mock_response = Mock()
                mock_response.raise_for_status.side_effect = Exception("404 Not Found")
                responses.append(("metadata", url))
                return mock_response
            else:
                # Second call - wheel request
                responses.append(("wheel", url))
                raise Exception("Wheel parsing intentionally mocked to fail")

        mock_session.get.side_effect = side_effect

        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"
        metadata_url = (
            "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl.metadata"
        )

        # This should raise an exception during wheel parsing, but we can verify the order
        try:
            get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url)
        except Exception:
            pass  # Expected to fail during wheel parsing mock

        # Verify that both URLs were called in the correct order
        assert len(responses) == 2
        assert responses[0] == ("metadata", metadata_url)
        assert responses[1] == ("wheel", wheel_url)
        assert mock_session.get.call_count == 2

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_without_pep658_behavior(
        self, mock_session: typing.Any
    ) -> None:
        """Test that without PEP 658 metadata URL, only wheel URL is called."""
        # Mock wheel request
        responses = []

        def side_effect(url: str) -> typing.Any:
            responses.append(("wheel", url))
            raise Exception("Wheel parsing intentionally mocked to fail")

        mock_session.get.side_effect = side_effect

        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"

        # This should raise an exception during wheel parsing, but we can verify the behavior
        try:
            get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url, metadata_url=None)
        except Exception:
            pass  # Expected to fail during wheel parsing mock

        # Verify that only the wheel URL was called
        assert len(responses) == 1
        assert responses[0] == ("wheel", wheel_url)
        mock_session.get.assert_called_once_with(wheel_url)

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_ignores_vendored_dist_info(
        self, mock_session: typing.Any
    ) -> None:
        """Test that METADATA of a vendored package is not used for the wheel."""
        # Arrange: the vendored dist-info comes first in the archive
        wheel_bytes = _make_wheel(
            {
                "vendored_lib-2.0.0.dist-info/METADATA": (
                    b"Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: vendored-lib\nVersion: 2.0.0\n"
                ),
                "test_package-1.0.0.dist-info/METADATA": (
                    b"Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: test-package\nVersion: 1.0.0\n"
                ),
            }
        )
        mock_session.get.return_value = Mock(content=wheel_bytes)
        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test_package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"

        # Act
        metadata = get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url)

        # Assert
        assert metadata.name == "test-package"
        assert str(metadata.version) == "1.0.0"

    @patch("fromager.candidate.session")
    def test_get_metadata_wheel_missing_expected_dist_info(
        self, mock_session: typing.Any
    ) -> None:
        """Test that a wheel without its own dist-info raises ValueError."""
        # Arrange: only a vendored dist-info is present
        wheel_bytes = _make_wheel(
            {
                "vendored_lib-2.0.0.dist-info/METADATA": (
                    b"Metadata-Version: 2.1\nName: vendored-lib\nVersion: 2.0.0\n"
                ),
            }
        )
        mock_session.get.return_value = Mock(content=wheel_bytes)
        wheel_url = "https://example.com/test_package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl"

        # Act / Assert
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="test_package-1.0.0.dist-info/METADATA"):
            get_metadata_for_wheel(wheel_url)

    def test_candidate_repr_with_metadata_url(self) -> None:
        """Test that Candidate representation includes metadata URL info."""
        candidate = Candidate(
            name="test-package",
            version=Version("1.0.0"),
            url="https://example.com/test-package-1.0.0-py3-none-any.whl",
            has_metadata=True,
        )

"""Requirement resolution for bootstrap process.

Handles PyPI and graph-based resolution strategies.
Git URL resolution stays in Bootstrapper (orchestration concern).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import threading
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version

from . import finders, resolver, sources, wheels
from .dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from .requirements_file import RequirementType

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from . import context

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class BootstrapRequirementResolver:
    """Resolve package requirements from PyPI or dependency graph during bootstrap.

    Single Responsibility: Coordinate resolution strategies for bootstrap process.
    Reason to Change: Resolution algorithm or provider priorities change.

    Resolution strategies (in order):
    1. Previous dependency graph (if available)
    2. PyPI lookup (via existing sources/resolver modules)

    Git URL resolution is NOT handled here - that stays in Bootstrapper
    because it requires BuildEnvironment and build dependencies.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        ctx: context.WorkContext,
        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
        multiple_versions: bool = False,
        cache_wheel_server_url: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize requirement resolver.

        Args:
            ctx: Work context with constraints and settings
            prev_graph: Optional previous dependency graph for caching
            multiple_versions: If ``True`` and no results are found through
                any other approach, takes the latest candidate from the
                cache server, ignoring the age filters.  In all other
                cases, returns an empty list when no candidates are found.
            cache_wheel_server_url: URL of the remote wheel cache server.
                Used as a fallback when age filtering produces no candidates.
        """
        self.ctx = ctx
        self.prev_graph = prev_graph
        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions
        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url
        # All known versions for a package, accumulated across resolution
        # contexts.  Versions discovered via different specifiers or req_types
        # are merged so that later lookups see the widest set.
        # Key: (normalized_name, pre_built)
        # Value: {version: url}
        self._known_versions: dict[tuple[NormalizedName, bool], dict[Version, str]] = {}
        # Requirement rules already resolved from network/graph.
        # Key: (str(req), pre_built)
        # Prevents redundant network calls for the same specifier.
        self._resolved_rules: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()
        # Protects _known_versions and _resolved_rules for thread safety.
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def resolve(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,
        pre_built: bool | None = None,
        return_all_versions: bool = False,
    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:
        """Resolve package requirement to matching version(s).

        Uses a two-step strategy:
        1. If this requirement rule has not been resolved before, fetch
           versions from the network (or previous graph) and extend the
           package-level known-versions cache.
        2. Filter all known versions for the package by the current
           requirement specifier.

        This ensures that versions discovered in one context (e.g.,
        top-level with cooldown bypass) are visible to later lookups
        with different specifiers for the same package.

        Args:
            req: Package requirement
            req_type: Type of requirement
            parent_req: Parent requirement from dependency chain
            pre_built: Optional override to force prebuilt (True) or source (False).
                If None (default), uses package build info to determine.
            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions. If False,
                return only the highest matching version.

        Returns:
            List of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).
            Contains one item when return_all_versions=False, or all matching
            versions when return_all_versions=True.

        """
        # Determine pre_built if not specified (needed for cache key)
        if pre_built is None:
            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)
            pre_built = pbi.pre_built

        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)

        with self._lock:
            if rule_key not in self._resolved_rules:
                # Rule not seen before — resolve from graph or network and
                # extend the package-level known-versions cache.
                self._resolve_and_extend(req, req_type, pre_built, parent_req)
                self._resolved_rules.add(rule_key)
            else:
                logger.debug(f"rule already resolved: {req}")

            # Filter all known versions by the current requirement specifier.
            matching = self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)

        if not matching:
            return []
        if return_all_versions:
            return matching
        return [matching[0]]

    def get_cached_resolution(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        pre_built: bool,
    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]] | None:
        """Return cached matching versions if this requirement was already resolved.

        Returns ``None`` if the requirement has not been resolved yet, allowing
        callers to distinguish between "no matching versions" and "not yet resolved".

        Args:
            req: Package requirement
            pre_built: Whether looking for prebuilt or source resolution

        Returns:
            List of (url, version) tuples if previously resolved, None otherwise.
        """
        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)
        with self._lock:
            if rule_key in self._resolved_rules:
                return self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)
        return None

    def _resolve_and_extend(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        pre_built: bool,
        parent_req: Requirement | None,
    ) -> None:
        """Resolve versions from graph/network and extend known versions cache."""
        # Try previous dependency graph
        cached_resolution = self._resolve_from_graph(
            req=req,
            req_type=req_type,
            pre_built=pre_built,
            parent_req=parent_req,
        )

        if cached_resolution:
            logger.debug(
                f"resolved from previous bootstrap: {len(cached_resolution)} version(s)"
            )
            results = cached_resolution
        elif pre_built:
            # Resolve prebuilt wheel
            wheel_server_urls = wheels.get_wheel_server_urls(
                self.ctx, req, cache_wheel_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL
            )
            results = wheels.resolve_all_prebuilt_wheels(
                ctx=self.ctx,
                req=req,
                wheel_server_urls=wheel_server_urls,
                req_type=req_type,
            )
        else:
            # Resolve source (sdist)
            provider = sources.get_source_provider(
                ctx=self.ctx,
                req=req,
                sdist_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL,
                req_type=req_type,
            )

A constraint is explicit user intent, so it overrides the age heuristic.\n                max_age_cutoff = None\n            results = resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider(","originalFile":"\"\"\"Requirement resolution for bootstrap process.\n\nHandles PyPI and graph-based resolution strategies.\nGit URL resolution stays in Bootstrapper (orchestration concern).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport threading\nimport typing\n\nfrom packaging.requirements import Requirement\nfrom packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name\nfrom packaging.version import Version\n\nfrom . import finders, resolver, sources, wheels\nfrom .dependency_graph import DependencyGraph\nfrom .requirements_file import RequirementType\n\nif typing.TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from . import context\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass BootstrapRequirementResolver:\n    \"\"\"Resolve package requirements from PyPI or dependency graph during bootstrap.\n\n    Single Responsibility: Coordinate resolution strategies for bootstrap process.\n    Reason to Change: Resolution algorithm or provider priorities change.\n\n    Resolution strategies (in order):\n    1. Previous dependency graph (if available)\n    2. PyPI lookup (via existing sources/resolver modules)\n\n    Git URL resolution is NOT handled here - that stays in Bootstrapper\n    because it requires BuildEnvironment and build dependencies.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        ctx: context.WorkContext,\n        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,\n        multiple_versions: bool = False,\n        cache_wheel_server_url: str = \"\",\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize requirement resolver.\n\n        Args:\n            ctx: Work context with constraints and settings\n            prev_graph: Optional previous dependency graph for caching\n            multiple_versions: If ``True`` and no results are found through\n                any other approach, takes the latest candidate from the\n                cache server, ignoring the age filters.  In all other\n                cases, returns an empty list when no candidates are found.\n            cache_wheel_server_url: URL of the remote wheel cache server.\n                Used as a fallback when age filtering produces no candidates.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.ctx = ctx\n        self.prev_graph = prev_graph\n        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions\n        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url\n        # All known versions for a package, accumulated across resolution\n        # contexts.  Versions discovered via different specifiers or req_types\n        # are merged so that later lookups see the widest set.\n        # Key: (normalized_name, pre_built)\n        # Value: {version: url}\n        self._known_versions: dict[tuple[NormalizedName, bool], dict[Version, str]] = {}\n        # Requirement rules already resolved from network/graph.\n        # Key: (str(req), pre_built)\n        # Prevents redundant network calls for the same specifier.\n        self._resolved_rules: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()\n        # Protects _known_versions and _resolved_rules for thread safety.\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def resolve(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,\n        pre_built: bool | None = None,\n        return_all_versions: bool = False,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Resolve package requirement to matching version(s).\n\n        Uses a two-step strategy:\n        1. If this requirement rule has not been resolved before, fetch\n           versions from the network (or previous graph) and extend the\n           package-level known-versions cache.\n        2. Filter all known versions for the package by the current\n           requirement specifier.\n\n        This ensures that versions discovered in one context (e.g.,\n        top-level with cooldown bypass) are visible to later lookups\n        with different specifiers for the same package.\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement\n            req_type: Type of requirement\n            parent_req: Parent requirement from dependency chain\n            pre_built: Optional override to force prebuilt (True) or source (False).\n                If None (default), uses package build info to determine.\n            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions. If False,\n                return only the highest matching version.\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).\n            Contains one item when return_all_versions=False, or all matching\n            versions when return_all_versions=True.\n\n        \"\"\"\n        # Determine pre_built if not specified (needed for cache key)\n        if pre_built is None:\n            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n            pre_built = pbi.pre_built\n\n        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)\n\n        with self._lock:\n            if rule_key not in self._resolved_rules:\n                # Rule not seen before — resolve from graph or network and\n                # extend the package-level known-versions cache.\n                self._resolve_and_extend(req, req_type, pre_built, parent_req)\n                self._resolved_rules.add(rule_key)\n            else:\n                logger.debug(f\"rule already resolved: {req}\")\n\n            # Filter all known versions by the current requirement specifier.\n            matching = self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)\n\n        if not matching:\n            return []\n        if return_all_versions:\n            return matching\n        return [matching[0]]\n\n    def get_cached_resolution(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        pre_built: bool,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]] | None:\n        \"\"\"Return cached matching versions if this requirement was already resolved.\n\n        Returns ``None`` if the requirement has not been resolved yet, allowing\n        callers to distinguish between \"no matching versions\" and \"not yet resolved\".\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement\n            pre_built: Whether looking for prebuilt or source resolution\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples if previously resolved, None otherwise.\n        \"\"\"\n        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)\n        with self._lock:\n            if rule_key in self._resolved_rules:\n                return self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)\n        return None\n\n    def _resolve_and_extend(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        pre_built: bool,\n        parent_req: Requirement | None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Resolve versions from graph/network and extend known versions cache.\"\"\"\n        # Try previous dependency graph\n        cached_resolution = self._resolve_from_graph(\n            req=req,\n            req_type=req_type,\n            pre_built=pre_built,\n            parent_req=parent_req,\n        )\n\n        if cached_resolution:\n            logger.debug(\n                f\"resolved from previous bootstrap: {len(cached_resolution)} version(s)\"\n            )\n            results = cached_resolution\n        elif pre_built:\n            # Resolve prebuilt wheel\n            wheel_server_urls = wheels.get_wheel_server_urls(\n                self.ctx, req, cache_wheel_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL\n            )\n            results = wheels.resolve_all_prebuilt_wheels(\n                ctx=self.ctx,\n                req=req,\n                wheel_server_urls=wheel_server_urls,\n                req_type=req_type,\n            )\n        else:\n            # Resolve source (sdist)\n            provider = sources.get_source_provider(\n                ctx=self.ctx,\n                req=req,\n                sdist_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL,\n                req_type=req_type,\n            )\n            max_age_cutoff = resolver._compute_max_age_cutoff(self.ctx)\n            results = resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider(\n                provider,\n                req,\n                max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff,\n                fallback_on_empty_age_filter=not self.multiple_versions,\n            )\n\n            if not results and self.multiple_versions and self.cache_wheel_server_url:\n                logger.info(\n                    \"no results found with normal resolution, \"\n                    \"falling back to the cache server %s\",\n                    self.cache_wheel_server_url,\n                )\n                results = self._resolve_from_cache_server(req)\n\n            if not results:\n                logger.warning(\n                    \"resolver returned no results \"\n                    \"(wheel server URL %s, %s version mode)\",\n                    self.cache_wheel_server_url or \"(none)\",\n                    \"multiple\" if self.multiple_versions else \"single\",\n                )\n\n        if results:\n            key = (canonicalize_name(req.name), pre_built)\n            versions = self._known_versions.setdefault(key, {})\n            for url, version in results:\n                if version not in versions or (url and not versions[version]):\n                    versions[version] = url\n            self._resolved_rules.add((str(req), pre_built))\n\n    def _resolve_from_cache_server(self, req: Requirement) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Fall back to the remote wheel cache server for a cached version.\n\n        When age filtering removes all candidates in multi-version mode,\n        queries the remote cache server for the newest available wheel.\n        Returns at most one version so that transitive dependencies are\n        re-processed without rebuilding every old version.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.info(\n            \"checking cache server %s for existing build\",\n            self.cache_wheel_server_url,\n        )\n        best: tuple[str, Version] | None = None\n        for include_sdists, include_wheels in [(False, True), (True, False)]:\n            try:\n                provider = Previous dependency graph (if available)\n    2. PyPI lookup (via existing sources/resolver modules)\n\n    Git URL resolution is NOT handled here - that stays in Bootstrapper\n    because it requires BuildEnvironment and build dependencies.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        ctx: context.WorkContext,\n        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,\n        multiple_versions: bool = False,\n        cache_wheel_server_url: str = \"\",\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize requirement resolver.\n\n        Args:\n            ctx: Work context with constraints and settings\n            prev_graph: Optional previous dependency graph for caching\n            multiple_versions: If ``True`` and no results are found through\n                any other approach, takes the latest candidate from the\n                cache server, ignoring the age filters.  In all other\n                cases, returns an empty list when no candidates are found.\n            cache_wheel_server_url: URL of the remote wheel cache server.\n                Used as a fallback when age filtering produces no candidates.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.ctx = ctx\n        self.prev_graph = prev_graph\n        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions\n        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url\n        # All known versions for a package, accumulated across resolution\n        # contexts.  Versions discovered via different specifiers or req_types\n        # are merged so that later lookups see the widest set.\n        # Key: (normalized_name, pre_built)\n        # Value: {version: url}\n        self._known_versions: dict[tuple[NormalizedName, bool], dict[Version, str]] = {}\n        # Requirement rules already resolved from network/graph.\n        # Key: (str(req), pre_built)\n        # Prevents redundant network calls for the same specifier.\n        self._resolved_rules: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()\n        # Protects _known_versions and _resolved_rules for thread safety.\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def resolve(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,\n        pre_built: bool | None = None,\n        return_all_versions: bool = False,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Resolve package requirement to matching version(s).\n\n        Uses a two-step strategy:\n        1. If this requirement rule has not been resolved before, fetch\n           versions from the network (or previous graph) and extend the\n           package-level known-versions cache.\n        2. Filter all known versions for the package by the current\n           requirement specifier.\n\n        This ensures that versions discovered in one context (e.g.,\n        top-level with cooldown bypass) are visible to later lookups\n        with different specifiers for the same package.\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement\n            req_type: Type of requirement\n            parent_req: Parent requirement from dependency chain\n            pre_built: Optional override to force prebuilt (True) or source (False).\n                If None (default), uses package build info to determine.\n            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions. If False,\n                return only the highest matching version.\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).\n            Contains one item when return_all_versions=False, or all matching\n            versions when return_all_versions=True.\n\n        \"\"\"\n        # Determine pre_built if not specified (needed for cache key)\n        if pre_built is None:\n            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n            pre_built = pbi.pre_built\n\n        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)\n\n        with self._lock:\n            if rule_key not in self._resolved_rules:\n                # Rule not seen before — resolve from graph or network and\n                # extend the package-level known-versions cache.\n                self._resolve_and_extend(req, req_type, pre_built, parent_req)\n                self._resolved_rules.add(rule_key)\n            else:\n                logger.debug(f\"rule already resolved: {req}\")\n\n            # Filter all known versions by the current requirement specifier.\n            matching = self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)\n\n        if not matching:\n            return []\n        if return_all_versions:\n            return matching\n        return [matching[0]]\n\n    def get_cached_resolution(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        pre_built: bool,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]] | None:\n        \"\"\"Return cached matching versions if this requirement was already resolved.\n\n        Returns ``None`` if the requirement has not been resolved yet, allowing\n        callers to distinguish between \"no matching versions\" and \"not yet resolved\".\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement\n            pre_built: Whether looking for prebuilt or source resolution\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples if previously resolved, None otherwise.\n        \"\"\"\n        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)\n        with self._lock:\n            if rule_key in self._resolved_rules:\n                return self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)\n        return None\n\n    def _resolve_and_extend(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        pre_built: bool,\n        parent_req: Requirement | None,\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Resolve versions from graph/network and extend known versions cache.\"\"\"\n        # Try previous dependency graph\n        cached_resolution = self._resolve_from_graph(\n            req=req,\n            req_type=req_type,\n            pre_built=pre_built,\n            parent_req=parent_req,\n        )\n\n        if cached_resolution:\n            logger.debug(\n                f\"resolved from previous bootstrap: {len(cached_resolution)} version(s)\"\n            )\n            results = cached_resolution\n        elif pre_built:\n            # Resolve prebuilt wheel\n            wheel_server_urls = wheels.get_wheel_server_urls(\n                self.ctx, req, cache_wheel_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL\n            )\n            results = wheels.resolve_all_prebuilt_wheels(\n                ctx=self.ctx,\n                req=req,\n                wheel_server_urls=wheel_server_urls,\n                req_type=req_type,\n            )\n        else:\n            # Resolve source (sdist)\n            provider = sources.get_source_provider(\n                ctx=self.ctx,\n                req=req,\n                sdist_server_url=resolver.PYPI_SERVER_URL,\n                req_type=req_type,\n            )\n            max_age_cutoff = resolver._compute_max_age_cutoff(self.ctx)\n            if self.ctx.constraints.get_constraint(req.name) is not None:\n                # A constraint is explicit user intent, so it overrides the age heuristic.\n                max_age_cutoff = None\n            results = resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider(\n                provider,\n                req,\n                max_age_cutoff=max_age_cutoff,\n                fallback_on_empty_age_filter=not self.multiple_versions,\n            )\n\n            if not results and self.multiple_versions and self.cache_wheel_server_url:\n                logger.info(\n                    \"no results found with normal resolution, \"\n                    \"falling back to the cache server %s\",\n                    self.cache_wheel_server_url,\n                )\n                results = self._resolve_from_cache_server(req)\n\n            if not results:\n                logger.warning(\n                    \"resolver returned no results \"\n                    \"(wheel server URL %s, %s version mode)\",\n                    self.cache_wheel_server_url or \"(none)\",\n                    \"multiple\" if self.multiple_versions else \"single\",\n                )\n\n        if results:\n            key = (canonicalize_name(req.name), pre_built)\n            versions = self._known_versions.setdefault(key, {})\n            for url, version in results:\n                if version not in versions or (url and not versions[version]):\n                    versions[version] = url\n            self._resolved_rules.add((str(req), pre_built))\n\n    def _resolve_from_cache_server(self, req: Requirement) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Fall back to the remote wheel cache server for a cached version.\n\n        When age filtering removes all candidates in multi-version mode,\n        queries the remote cache server for the newest available wheel.\n        Returns at most one version so that transitive dependencies are\n        re-processed without rebuilding every old version.\n        \"\"\"\n        logger.info(\n            \"checking cache server %s for existing build\",\n            self.cache_wheel_server_url,\n        )\n        best: tuple[str, Version] | None = None\n        for include_sdists, include_wheels in [(False, True), (True, False)]:\n            try:\n                provider = finders.PyPICacheProvider(\n                    cache_server_url=self.cache_wheel_server_url,\n                    constraints=self.ctx.constraints,\n                    include_sdists=include_sdists,\n                    include_wheels=include_wheels,\n                )\n                results = resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider(provider, req)\n                if results:\n                    url, version = results[0]\n                    if best is None or version > best[1]:\n                        best = (url, version)\n            except Exception as err:\n                logger.warning(\n                    \"error checking cache server %s: %s\",\n                    self.cache_wheel_server_url,\n                    err,\n                )\n        if best is not None:\n            logger.info(\"found version %s on cache server\", best[1])\n            return [best]\n        return []\n\n    def get_matching_versions(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        pre_built: bool,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Filter known versions by requirement specifier (thread-safe).\n\n        Returns all known versions of the package that satisfy the\n        requirement's version specifier, sorted highest-first.\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement with version specifier\n            pre_built: Whether looking for prebuilt or source resolution\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples matching the specifier.\n        \"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            return self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)\n\n    def _get_matching_versions(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        pre_built: bool,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Filter known versions (caller must hold ``self._lock``).\"\"\"\n        key = (canonicalize_name(req.name), pre_built)\n        versions = self._known_versions.get(key, {})\n        matching = [\n            (url, version)\n            for version, url in versions.items()\n            if version in req.specifier\n        ]\n        matching.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)\n        return matching\n\n    def _resolve_from_graph(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        pre_built: bool,\n        parent_req: Requirement | None,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]] | None:\n        \"\"\"Resolve from previous dependency graph.\n\n        Extracted from Bootstrapper._resolve_from_graph().\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples if found in graph, None otherwise\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self.prev_graph:\n            return None\n\n        seen_version: set[str] = """Tests for multiple versions feature in bootstrap_requirement_resolver."""

import datetime
from pathlib import Path
from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.version import Version

from fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver import BootstrapRequirementResolver
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType


@pytest.fixture
def tmp_context(tmp_path: Path) -> WorkContext:
    """Create a minimal WorkContext for testing."""
    ctx = MagicMock(spec=WorkContext)
    ctx.work_dir = tmp_path
    ctx.constraints = MagicMock()
    ctx.constraints.get_constraint.return_value = None
    ctx.settings = MagicMock()
    ctx.settings.list_pre_built.return_value = set()
    ctx.package_build_info = MagicMock()
    pbi = MagicMock()
    pbi.pre_built = False
    pbi.resolver_include_sdists = True
    pbi.resolver_include_wheels = False
    pbi.resolver_ignore_platform = False
    pbi.resolver_sdist_server_url.return_value = "https://pypi.org/simple/"
    ctx.package_build_info.return_value = pbi
    ctx.max_release_age = None
    return ctx


_MOCK_VERSIONS = [
    ("https://pypi.org/testpkg-2.0.tar.gz", Version("2.0")),
    ("https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.5.tar.gz", Version("1.5")),
    ("https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz", Version("1.0")),
]


def test_resolve_return_all_versions_true(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """resolve() with return_all_versions=True returns all matching versions."""
    brr = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)

    with (
        patch.object(brr, "_resolve_from_graph", return_value=None),
        patch(
            "fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.sources.get_source_provider",
        ),
        patch(
            "fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.resolver"
            ".find_all_matching_from_provider",
            return_value=list(_MOCK_VERSIONS),
        ),
    ):
        req = Requirement("testpkg>=1.0")
        results = brr.resolve(
            req=req,
            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
            parent_req=None,
            return_all_versions=True,
        )

        assert len(results) == 3
        assert results[0] == _MOCK_VERSIONS[0]
        assert results[1] == _MOCK_VERSIONS[1]
        assert results[2] == _MOCK_VERSIONS[2]


def test_resolve_return_all_versions_false_default(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """resolve() with return_all_versions=False (default) returns list with only highest version."""
    brr = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)

    with (
        patch.object(brr, "_resolve_from_graph", return_value=None),
        patch(
            "fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.sources.get_source_provider",
        ),
        patch(
            "fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.resolver"
            ".find_all_matching_from_provider",
            return_value=list(_MOCK_VERSIONS),
        ),
    ):
        req = Requirement("testpkg>=1.0")
        results = brr.resolve(
            req=req,
            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
            parent_req=None,
        )

        assert len(results) == 1
        assert results[0] == _MOCK_VERSIONS[0]


def test_resolve_return_all_versions_uses_cache(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """resolve() with return_all_versions=True uses cache correctly."""
    brr = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)

    with (
        patch.object(brr, "_resolve_from_graph", return_value=None),
        patch(
            "fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.sources.get_source_provider",
        ),
        patch(
            "fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.resolver"
            ".find_all_matching_from_provider",
            return_value=[
                ("https://pypi.org/testpkg-2.0.tar.gz", Version("2.0")),
                ("https://pypi.org/testpkg-1.0.tar.gz", Version("1.0")),
            ],
        ) as mock_resolve,
    ):
        req = Requirement("testpkg>=1.0")

        results1 = brr.resolve(
            req=req,
            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
            parent_req=None,
            return_all_versions=True,
        )
        assert len(results1) == 2
        assert mock_resolve.call_count == 1

        results2 = brr.resolve(
            req=req,
            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
            parent_req=None,
            return_all_versions=True,
        )

        # Should not call resolution again — cache hit
        assert mock_resolve.call_count == 1
        assert results2 == results1


def test_resolve_return_all_versions_with_previous_graph(

    prev_graph = DependencyGraph()
    prev_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,

        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,

        parent_req=None,
        return_all_versions=True,
    )

    assert len(results) == 2
    versions = [v for _, v in results]
    assert Version("2.0") in versions
    assert Version("1.0") in versions

"""Requirement resolution for bootstrap process.

Handles PyPI and graph-based resolution strategies.
Git URL resolution stays in Bootstrapper (orchestration concern).
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import threading
import typing

from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from . import finders, resolver, sources, wheels
from .dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from .requirements_file import RequirementType

if typing.TYPE_CHECKING:
    from . import context

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class BootstrapRequirementResolver:
    """Resolve package requirements from PyPI or dependency graph during bootstrap.

    Single Responsibility: Coordinate resolution strategies for bootstrap process.
    Reason to Change: Resolution algorithm or provider priorities change.

    Resolution strategies (in order):
    1. Previous dependency graph (if available)
    2. PyPI lookup (via existing sources/resolver modules)

    Git URL resolution is NOT handled here - that stays in Bootstrapper
    because it requires BuildEnvironment and build dependencies.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        ctx: context.WorkContext,
        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,
        multiple_versions: bool = False,
        cache_wheel_server_url: str = "",
    ) -> None:
        """Initialize requirement resolver.

        Args:
            ctx: Work context with constraints and settings
            prev_graph: Optional previous dependency graph for caching
            multiple_versions: If ``True`` and no results are found through
                any other approach, takes the latest candidate from the
                cache server, ignoring the age filters.  In all other
                cases, returns an empty list when no candidates are found.
            cache_wheel_server_url: URL of the remote wheel cache server.
                Used as a fallback when age filtering produces no candidates.
        """
        self.ctx = ctx
        self.prev_graph = prev_graph
        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions
        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url
        # All known versions for a package, accumulated across resolution
        # contexts.  Versions discovered via different specifiers or req_types
        # are merged so that later lookups see the widest set.
        # Key: (normalized_name, pre_built)
        # Value: {version: url}
        self._known_versions: dict[tuple[NormalizedName, bool], dict[Version, str]] = {}
        # Requirement rules already resolved from network/graph.
        # Key: (str(req), pre_built)
        # Prevents redundant network calls for the same specifier.
        self._resolved_rules: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()
        # Protects _known_versions and _resolved_rules for thread safety.
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def resolve(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,
        pre_built: bool | None = None,
        return_all_versions: bool = False,
    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:
        """Resolve package requirement to matching version(s).

        Uses a two-step strategy:
        1. If this requirement rule has not been resolved before, fetch
           versions from the network (or previous graph) and extend the
           package-level known-versions cache.
        2. Filter all known versions for the package by the current
           requirement specifier.

        This ensures that versions discovered in one context (e.g.,
        top-level with cooldown bypass) are visible to later lookups
        with different specifiers for the same package.

        Args:
            req: Package requirement
            req_type: Type of requirement
            parent_req: Parent requirement from dependency chain
            pre_built: Optional override to force prebuilt (True) or source (False).
                If None (default), uses package build info to determine.
            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions. If False,
                return only the highest matching version.

        Returns:
            List of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).
            Contains one item when return_all_versions=False, or all matching
            versions when return_all_versions=True.

        Raises:
            ValueError: If req contains a git URL and pre_built is False
                (git URL source resolution must be handled by Bootstrapper)
        """
        # Determine pre_built if not specified (needed for cache key and URL guard)
        if pre_built is None:
            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)
            pre_built = pbi.pre_built

        # Check session cache BEFORE the git URL guard so that background
        # threads can retrieve pre-cached git URL resolutions (populated by
        # Bootstrapper.resolve_versions() on the main thread before bootstrap()
        # is called) without hitting the ValueError.
        cached_result = self.get_cached_resolution(req, pre_built)
        if cached_result is not None:
            logger.debug(f"resolved {req} from cache")
            return list(cached_result) if return_all_versions else [cached_result[0]]

        # Git URL source resolution must be handled by Bootstrapper.
        # But git URL prebuilt resolution is allowed - we look for wheels on PyPI
        # (test mode fallback uses this path).
        if req.url and not pre_built:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Git URL requirements must be handled by Bootstrapper: {req}"
            )

        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)

        with self._lock:
            if rule_key not in self._resolved_rules:
                # Rule not seen before — resolve from graph or network and
                # extend the package-level known-versions cache.
                try:
                    self._resolve_and_extend(req, req_type, pre_built, parent_req)
                except ResolverException as err:
                    # Name the parent that asked for this requirement, so the
                    # error points at the broken arc, not the top-level package
                    # that happens to be active in the logging context.
                    if parent_req is None:
                        raise
                    raise ResolverException(
                        f"{req} required by {parent_req.name} cannot be resolved: {err}"
                    ) from err
                self._resolved_rules.add(rule_key)
            else:
                logger.debug(f"rule already resolved: {req}")

            # Filter all known versions by the current requirement specifier.
            matching = self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)

        if not matching:
            return []
        if return_all_versions:
            return matching
        return [matching[0]]

    def get_cached_resolution(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        pre_built: bool,
    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]] | None:
        """Return cached matching versions if this requirement was already resolved.

        Returns ``None`` if the requirement has not been resolved yet, allowing
        callers to distinguish between "no matching versions" and "not yet resolved".

        Used by background threads to retrieve pre-cached git URL resolutions
        populated by the main thread before entering the parallel section.

        Args:
            req: Package requirement
            pre_built: Whether looking for prebuilt or source resolution

        Returns:
            List of (url, version) tuples if previously resolved, None otherwise.
        """
        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)
        with self._lock:
            if rule_key in self._resolved_rules:
                return self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)
        return None

    def _resolve_and_extend(
        self,
        req: Requirement,
        req_type: RequirementType,
        pre_built: bool,
        parent_req: Requirement | None,

+def test_resolve_failure_names_parent_that_required_requirement(
+    tmp_context: WorkContext,
+) -> None:
+    """A failed dependency resolution names the parent that required it.
+
+    vllm requires flashinfer-python, which cannot be resolved. The error must
+    blame vllm, the broken arc, not the top-level package active in the logs.
+    """
+    # Arrange
+    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, prev_graph=None)
+    failure = ResolverException("no candidates match")
+
+    # Act
+    with (
+        patch.object(resolver, "_resolve_and_extend", side_effect=failure),
+        pytest.raises(ResolverException) as exc_info,
+    ):
+        resolver.resolve(
+            req=Requirement("flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1"),
+            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
+            parent_req=Requirement("vllm"),
+            pre_built=False,
+        )
+
+    # Assert
+    message = str(exc_info.value)
+    assert "flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1 required by vllm" in message
+    assert "no candidates match" in message
+    assert exc_info.value.__cause__ is failure

_run_bootstrap_loop(self, stack: list[Phase]) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Run the iterative DFS bootstrap loop over a pre-built work stack.\n\n        Pops items one at a time, dispatches each phase, and pushes any\n        follow-on items (continuations and new dependencies) back onto the\n        stack. Updates the progress bar as items complete.\n\n        Args:\n            stack: Initial list of ``Phase`` objects to process. Modified\n                in-place; empty on return.\n        \"\"\"\n        while stack:\n            self._record_stack_state(stack)\n            item = stack.pop()\n            self.why = list(item.work_item.why_snapshot)\n\n            with (\n                req_ctxvar_context(item.work_item.req, item.work_item.resolved_version),\n                self._track_why(item),\n            ):\n                if item.requires_exclusive_run:\n                    logger.info(\n                        \"%s requires exclusive build, draining background pool\",\n                        item.work_item.req,\n                    )\n                    self._drain_background_pool()\n                try:\n                    new_items = item.run(self)\n                except Exception as err:\n                    new_items = self._handle_phase_error(item, err)\n\n            new_dep_count = sum(1 for it in new_items if isinstance(it, Resolve))\n            if new_dep_count > 0:\n                self.progressbar.update_total(new_dep_count)\n            if not new_items:\n                self.progressbar.update()\n\n            self._push_items(stack, new_items)\n\n    def _bootstrap_one(self, req: Requirement, req_type: RequirementType) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Bootstrap a single requirement using an iterative DFS loop.\n\n        Internal method used only by the git URL resolution path\n        (``_handle_build_requirements``). All other callers should use\n        ``bootstrap(requirements)`` instead.\n\n        Uses an explicit LIFO stack instead of recursion to handle arbitrarily\n        deep dependency graphs without hitting Python's recursion limit.\n----\n        req: Requirement,\n        build_type: RequirementType,\n        build_dependencies: set[Requirement],\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Bootstrap build dependencies.\n\n        Only used by the git URL resolution path\n        (_resolve_version_from_git_url -> _get_version_from_package_metadata).\n        The main iterative bootstrap loop handles build deps via phase handlers.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.progressbar.update_total(len(build_dependencies))\n\n        for dep in self._sort_requirements(build_dependencies):\n            with req_ctxvar_context(dep):\n                # Save/restore self.why because the iterative bootstrap()\n                # modifies it internally for each work item.\n                saved_why = list(self.why)\n                self._bootstrap_one(req=dep, req_type=build_type)\n                self.why = saved_why\n            self.progressbar.update()\n\n    def _download_prebuilt(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        resolved_version: Version,\n        wheel_url: str,\n    ) -> tuple[pathlib.Path, pathlib.Path]:\n        result = _cache._bg_prepare_prebuilt(\n            self.ctx, req, req_type, resolved_version, wheel_url\n        )","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01Az47wv954EtAcM3vmmY86r","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"rule"}}]}

A new dependency (wheel) also requires packaging>=24.0.\n    Because wheel is not in the previous graph, the parent-specific lookup fails\n    and fromager falls back to PyPI, picking up packaging==26.0 instead of reusing 25.0.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Build a previous graph that mirrors the real-world scenario:\n    # ROOT -> setuptools-scm==9.2.2 --[install]--> packaging==25.0\n    prev_graph = DependencyGraph()\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=None,\n        parent_version=None,\n        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n        req=Requirement(\"setuptools-scm\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"9.2.2\"),\n    )\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=canonicalize_name(\"setuptools-scm\"),\n        parent_version=Version(\"9.2.2\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        req=Requirement(\"packaging>=20\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"25.0\"),\n    )\n\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, prev_graph)\n\n    # Resolve packaging>=24.0 via a NEW parent \"wheel\" that is NOT in prev_graph.\n    # packaging==25.0 satisfies >=24.0 and exists in the graph, so it should\n    # be returned instead of falling back to PyPI.\n    result = resolver._resolve_from_graph(\n        req=Requirement(\"packaging>=24.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        pre_built=False,\n        parent_req=Requirement(\"wheel\"),\n    )\n    assert result is not None, (\n        \"Expected packaging==25.0 from prev_graph but got None (would fall back to PyPI)\"\n    )\n    assert result == [(\"\", Version(\"25.0\"))]\n\n\ndef test_resolve_from_graph_different_req_type_reuses_existing_version(\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:","stderr":"","interrupted":false,"isImage":false,"noOutputExpected":false},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01BYzyofmk6BDuUr5uhAjuSu","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"rule"}}]}

Name the parent that asked for this requirement, so the\n                    # error points at the broken arc, not the top-level package\n                    # that happens to be active in the logging context.\n                    if parent_req is None:\n                        raise\n                    raise ResolverException(\n                        f\"{req} required by {parent_req.name} cannot be resolved: {err}\"\n                    ) from err\n                self._resolved_rules.add(rule_key)","originalFile":"\"\"\"Requirement resolution for bootstrap process.\n\nHandles PyPI and graph-based resolution strategies.\nGit URL resolution stays in Bootstrapper (orchestration concern).\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport logging\nimport threading\nimport typing\n\nfrom packaging.requirements import Requirement\nfrom packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name\nfrom packaging.version import Version\n\nfrom . import finders, resolver, sources, wheels\nfrom .dependency_graph import DependencyGraph\nfrom .requirements_file import RequirementType\n\nif typing.TYPE_CHECKING:\n    from . import context\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\n\n\nclass BootstrapRequirementResolver:\n    \"\"\"Resolve package requirements from PyPI or dependency graph during bootstrap.\n\n    Single Responsibility: Coordinate resolution strategies for bootstrap process.\n    Reason to Change: Resolution algorithm or provider priorities change.\n\n    Resolution strategies (in order):\n    1. Previous dependency graph (if available)\n    2. PyPI lookup (via existing sources/resolver modules)\n\n    Git URL resolution is NOT handled here - that stays in Bootstrapper\n    because it requires BuildEnvironment and build dependencies.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(\n        self,\n        ctx: context.WorkContext,\n        prev_graph: DependencyGraph | None = None,\n        multiple_versions: bool = False,\n        cache_wheel_server_url: str = \"\",\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Initialize requirement resolver.\n\n        Args:\n            ctx: Work context with constraints and settings\n            prev_graph: Optional previous dependency graph for caching\n            multiple_versions: If ``True`` and no results are found through\n                any other approach, takes the latest candidate from the\n                cache server, ignoring the age filters.  In all other\n                cases, returns an empty list when no candidates are found.\n            cache_wheel_server_url: URL of the remote wheel cache server.\n                Used as a fallback when age filtering produces no candidates.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.ctx = ctx\n        self.prev_graph = prev_graph\n        self.multiple_versions = multiple_versions\n        self.cache_wheel_server_url = cache_wheel_server_url\n        # All known versions for a package, accumulated across resolution\n        # contexts.  Versions discovered via different specifiers or req_types\n        # are merged so that later lookups see the widest set.\n        # Key: (normalized_name, pre_built)\n        # Value: {version: url}\n        self._known_versions: dict[tuple[NormalizedName, bool], dict[Version, str]] = {}\n        # Requirement rules already resolved from network/graph.\n        # Key: (str(req), pre_built)\n        # Prevents redundant network calls for the same specifier.\n        self._resolved_rules: set[tuple[str, bool]] = set()\n        # Protects _known_versions and _resolved_rules for thread safety.\n        self._lock = threading.Lock()\n\n    def resolve(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        parent_req: Requirement | None = None,\n        pre_built: bool | None = None,\n        return_all_versions: bool = False,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Resolve package requirement to matching version(s).\n\n        Uses a two-step strategy:\n        1. If this requirement rule has not been resolved before, fetch\n           versions from the network (or previous graph) and extend the\n           package-level known-versions cache.\n        2. Filter all known versions for the package by the current\n           requirement specifier.\n\n        This ensures that versions discovered in one context (e.g.,\n        top-level with cooldown bypass) are visible to later lookups\n        with different specifiers for the same package.\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement\n            req_type: Type of requirement\n            parent_req: Parent requirement from dependency chain\n            pre_built: Optional override to force prebuilt (True) or source (False).\n                If None (default), uses package build info to determine.\n            return_all_versions: If True, return all matching versions. If False,\n                return only the highest matching version.\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples sorted by version (highest first).\n            Contains one item when return_all_versions=False, or all matching\n            versions when return_all_versions=True.\n\n        Raises:\n            ValueError: If req contains a git URL and pre_built is False\n                (git URL source resolution must be handled by Bootstrapper)\n        \"\"\"\n        # Determine pre_built if not specified (needed for cache key and URL guard)\n        if pre_built is None:\n            pbi = self.ctx.package_build_info(req)\n            pre_built = pbi.pre_built\n\n        # Check session cache BEFORE the git URL guard so that background\n        # threads can retrieve pre-cached git URL resolutions (populated by\n        # Bootstrapper.resolve_versions() on the main thread before bootstrap()\n        # is called) without hitting the ValueError.\n        cached_result = self.get_cached_resolution(req, pre_built)\n        if cached_result is not None:\n            logger.debug(f\"resolved {req} from cache\")\n            return list(cached_result) if return_all_versions else [cached_result[0]]\n\n        # Git URL source resolution must be handled by Bootstrapper.\n        # But git URL prebuilt resolution is allowed - we look for wheels on PyPI\n        # (test mode fallback uses this path).\n        if req.url and not pre_built:\n            raise ValueError(\n                f\"Git URL requirements must be handled by Bootstrapper: {req}\"\n            )\n\n        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)\n\n        with self._lock:\n            if rule_key not in self._resolved_rules:\n                # Rule not seen before — resolve from graph or network and\n                # extend the package-level known-versions cache.\n                self._resolve_and_extend(req, req_type, pre_built, parent_req)\n                self._resolved_rules.add(rule_key)\n            else:\n                logger.debug(f\"rule already resolved: {req}\")\n\n            # Filter all known versions by the current requirement specifier.\n            matching = self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)\n\n        if not matching:\n            return []\n        if return_all_versions:\n            return matching\n        return [matching[0]]\n\n    def get_cached_resolution(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        pre_built: bool,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]] | None:\n        \"\"\"Return cached matching versions if this requirement was already resolved.\n\n        Returns ``None`` if the requirement has not been resolved yet, allowing\n        callers to distinguish between \"no matching versions\" and \"not yet resolved\".\n\n        Used by background threads to retrieve pre-cached git URL resolutions\n        populated by the main thread before entering the parallel section.\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement\n            pre_built: Whether looking for prebuilt or source resolution\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples if previously resolved, None otherwise.\n        \"\"\"\n        rule_key = (str(req), pre_built)\n        with self._lock:\n            if rule_key in self._resolved_rules:\n                return self._get_matching_versions(req, pre_built)\n        return None\n\n    def _resolve_and_extend(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        pre_built:
