Requirement,\n        pre_built: bool,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]]:\n        \"\"\"Filter known versions (caller must hold ``self._lock``).\"\"\"\n        key = (canonicalize_name(req.name), pre_built)\n        versions = self._known_versions.get(key, {})\n        matching = [\n            (url, version)\n            for version, url in versions.items()\n            if version in req.specifier\n        ]\n        matching.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)\n        return matching\n\n    def extend_known_versions(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        pre_built: bool,\n        result: list[tuple[str, Version]],\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Extend the known-versions cache and mark the rule as resolved (thread-safe).\n\n        Merges new versions into the package-level cache. When a version\n        already exists, a non-empty URL takes precedence over an empty one\n        (graph-resolved placeholders are replaced by real download URLs).\n\n        Used by Bootstrapper to cache git URL resolutions that are\n        handled externally (outside this resolver).\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement (used for name and rule tracking)\n            pre_built: Whether this is a prebuilt or source resolution\n            result: List of (url, version) tuples to add\n        \"\"\"\n        with self._lock:\n            self._extend_known_versions(req, pre_built, result)\n\n    def _extend_known_versions(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        pre_built: bool,\n        result: list[tuple[str, Version]],\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Extend known versions (caller must hold ``self._lock``).\"\"\"\n        key = (canonicalize_name(req.name), pre_built)\n        versions = self._known_versions.setdefault(key, {})\n        for url, version in result:\n            if version not in versions or (url and not versions[version]):\n                versions[version] = url\n        self._resolved_rules.add((str(req), pre_built))\n\n    def _resolve_from_graph(\n        self,\n        req: Requirement,\n        req_type: RequirementType,\n        pre_built: bool,\n        parent_req: Requirement | None,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]] | None:\n        \"\"\"Resolve from previous dependency graph.\n\n        Extracted from Bootstrapper._resolve_from_graph().\n\n        Args:\n            req: Package requirement\n            req_type: Type of requirement\n            pre_built: Whether to look for pre-built packages\n            parent_req: Parent requirement for graph traversal\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples if found in graph, None otherwise\n        \"\"\"\n        if not self.prev_graph:\n            return None\n\n        seen_version: set[str] = set()\n\n        # First perform resolution using the top level reqs before looking at history\n        possible_versions_in_top_level: list[tuple[str, Version]] = []\n        for (\n            top_level_edge\n        ) in self.ctx.dependency_graph.get_root_node().get_outgoing_edges(\n            req.name, RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL\n        ):\n            possible_versions_in_top_level.append(\n                (\n                    top_level_edge.destination_node.download_url,\n                    top_level_edge.destination_node.version,\n                )\n            )\n            seen_version.add(str(top_level_edge.destination_node.version))\n\n        resolver_result = self._resolve_from_version_source(\n            possible_versions_in_top_level, req\n        )\n        if resolver_result:\n            return resolver_result\n\n        # Only if there is nothing in top level reqs, resolve using history\n        possible_versions_from_graph: list[tuple[str, Version]] = []\n        # Check all nodes which have the same parent name irrespective of the parent's version\n        for parent_node in self.prev_graph.get_nodes_by_name(\n            parent_req.name if parent_req else None\n        ):\n            # If the edge matches the current req and type then it is a possible candidate.\n            # Filtering on type might not be necessary, but we are being safe here. This will\n            # for sure ensure that bootstrap takes the same route as it did in the previous one.\n            # If we don't filter by type then it might pick up a different version from a different\n            # type that should have appeared much later in the resolution process.\n            for edge in parent_node.get_outgoing_edges(req.name, req_type):\n                if (\n                    edge.destination_node.pre_built == pre_built\n                    and str(edge.destination_node.version) not in seen_version\n                ):\n                    possible_versions_from_graph.append(\n                        (\n                            edge.destination_node.download_url,\n                            edge.destination_node.version,\n                        )\n                    )\n                    seen_version.add(str(edge.destination_node.version))\n\n        resolver_result = self._resolve_from_version_source(\n            possible_versions_from_graph, req\n        )\n        if resolver_result:\n            return resolver_result\n\n        # Fallback: search by package name across the entire previous graph,\n        # ignoring parent and req_type.  This handles cases where a dependency\n        # is encountered via a new parent or a different req_type that did not\n        # exist in the previous graph (#958).\n        # NOTE: This fallback ignores both parent and req_type filters.\n        # It may pick a version from a different parent or dependency type\n        # than the original bootstrap order, but this is preferable to\n        # falling through to PyPI and pulling an unpinned version.\n        possible_versions_by_name: list[tuple[str, Version]] = []\n        for node in self.prev_graph.get_nodes_by_name(req.name):\n            if node.pre_built == pre_built and str(node.version) not in seen_version:\n                possible_versions_by_name.append((node.download_url, node.version))\n                seen_version.add(str(node.version))\n\n        if possible_versions_by_name:\n            logger.debug(\n                \"%s: name-based fallback found versions in previous graph: %s\",\n                req.name,\n                [str(v) for _, v in possible_versions_by_name],\n            )\n        else:\n            logger.debug(\n                \"%s: no versions found in previous graph by name either\",\n                req.name,\n            )\n\n        return self._resolve_from_version_source(possible_versions_by_name, req)\n\n    def _resolve_from_version_source(\n        self,\n        version_source: list[tuple[str, Version]],\n        req: Requirement,\n    ) -> list[tuple[str, Version]] | None:\n        \"\"\"Filter and return all matching versions from candidates.\n\n        Extracted from Bootstrapper._resolve_from_version_source().\n\n        Args:\n            version_source: List of (url, version) candidates\n            req: Package requirement with version specifier\n\n        Returns:\n            List of (url, version) tuples for all matches, None if no matches\n        \"\"\"\n        if not version_source:\n            return None\n        try:\n            # No need to pass req type to enable caching since we are already using the graph as our cache.\n            # Do not cache candidates.\n            provider = resolver.GenericProvider(\n                version_source=lambda identifier: version_source,\n                constraints=self.ctx.constraints,\n                use_resolver_cache=False,\n            )\n            # find_all_matching_from_provider now returns all matching candidates\n            return resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider(provider, req)\n        except Exception as err:\n            logger.debug(f\"could not resolve {req} from {version_source}: {err}\")\n            return None\n","structuredPatch":[{"oldStart":13,"oldLines":6,"newStart":13,"newLines":7,"lines":[" from packaging.requirements import Requirement"," from packaging.utils import NormalizedName, canonicalize_name"," from packaging.version import Version","+from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException"," "," from . import finders, resolver, sources, wheels"," from .dependency_graph import DependencyGraph"]}],"userModified":false,"replaceAll":false,"contentNotInModelContext":true},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01MpwLKzEi64714kmMuKcwEa","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"rule"}}]}

Build a previous graph that mirrors the real-world scenario:\n    # ROOT -> setuptools-scm==9.2.2 --[install]--> packaging==25.0\n    prev_graph = DependencyGraph()\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=None,\n        parent_version=None,\n        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n        req=Requirement(\"setuptools-scm\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"9.2.2\"),\n    )\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=canonicalize_name(\"setuptools-scm\"),\n        parent_version=Version(\"9.2.2\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        req=Requirement(\"packaging>=20\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"25.0\"),\n    )\n\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, prev_graph)\n\n    # Resolve packaging>=24.0 via a NEW parent \"wheel\" that is NOT in prev_graph.\n    # packaging==25.0 satisfies >=24.0 and exists in the graph, so it should\n    # be returned instead of falling back to PyPI.\n    result = resolver._resolve_from_graph(\n        req=Requirement(\"packaging>=24.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        pre_built=False,\n        parent_req=Requirement(\"wheel\"),\n    )\n    assert result is not None, (\n        \"Expected packaging==25.0 from prev_graph but got None (would fall back to PyPI)\"\n    )\n    assert result == [(\"\", Version(\"25.0\"))]\n\n\ndef test_resolve_from_graph_different_req_type_reuses_existing_version(\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Graph resolution finds a package even when req_type differs.\n\n    If a package appears as a build-system dependency in the previous graph\n    but is now encountered as an install dependency (or vice-versa), the\n    strict req_type filter causes the lookup to fail, falling back to PyPI\n    and potentially picking up a newer version.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Previous graph: foo==1.0 --[build-system]--> bar==2.0\n    prev_graph = DependencyGraph()\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=None,\n        parent_version=None,\n        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n        req=Requirement(\"foo\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"1.0\"),\n    )\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=canonicalize_name(\"foo\"),\n        parent_version=Version(\"1.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.BUILD_SYSTEM,\n        req=Requirement(\"bar>=1.0\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"2.0\"),\n    )\n\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, prev_graph)\n\n    # Now resolve bar>=1.5 as an INSTALL dep of foo (different req_type).\n    # bar==2.0 satisfies >=1.5 and exists in the graph under the same parent\n    # but with a different req_type.\n    result = resolver._resolve_from_graph(\n        req=Requirement(\"bar>=1.5\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        pre_built=False,\n        parent_req=Requirement(\"foo\"),\n    )\n    assert result is not None, (\n        \"Expected bar==2.0 from prev_graph but got None (would fall back to PyPI)\"\n    )\n    assert result == [(\"\", Version(\"2.0\"))]\n\n\ndef test_resolve_from_graph_parent_specific_preferred_over_name_fallback(\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Parent-specific lookup is preferred over the name-based fallback.\n\n    When the previous graph contains a package under the exact parent and\n    req_type being requested, the parent-specific result must be returned\n    even though the name-based fallback would also find candidates.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Previous graph:\n    #   ROOT -> foo==1.0 --[install]--> bar==2.0\n    #   ROOT -> baz==1.0 --[install]--> bar==3.0\n    prev_graph = DependencyGraph()\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=None,\n        parent_version=None,\n        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n        req=Requirement(\"foo\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"1.0\"),\n    )\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=canonicalize_name(\"foo\"),\n        parent_version=Version(\"1.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        req=Requirement(\"bar>=1.0\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"2.0\"),\n    )\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=None,\n        parent_version=None,\n        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n        req=Requirement(\"baz\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"1.0\"),\n    )\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=canonicalize_name(\"baz\"),\n        parent_version=Version(\"1.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        req=Requirement(\"bar>=1.0\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"3.0\"),\n    )\n\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, prev_graph)\n\n    # Resolve bar>=1.0 as install dep of foo.  The parent-specific lookup\n    # should return bar==2.0 (from foo), NOT bar==3.0 (from baz via fallback).\n    result = resolver._resolve_from_graph(\n        req=Requirement(\"bar>=1.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        pre_built=False,\n        parent_req=Requirement(\"foo\"),\n    )\n    assert result is not None\n    assert result == [(\"\", Version(\"2.0\"))]\n\n\ndef test_resolve_from_graph_name_fallback_returns_none_for_missing_package(\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Name-based fallback returns None when the package is not in the graph.\n\n    When the previous graph is populated but does not contain the requested\n    package under any parent or req_type, both the parent-specific lookup\n    and the name-based fallback should return None so that resolution\n    proceeds to PyPI.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Previous graph has packages, but NOT \"missing-pkg\".\n    prev_graph = DependencyGraph()\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=None,\n        parent_version=None,\n        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n        req=Requirement(\"foo\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"1.0\"),\n    )\n    prev_graph.add_dependency(\n        parent_name=canonicalize_name(\"foo\"),\n        parent_version=Version(\"1.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        req=Requirement(\"bar>=1.0\"),\n        req_version=Version(\"2.0\"),\n    )\n\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, prev_graph)\n\n    result = resolver._resolve_from_graph(\n        req=Requirement(\"missing-pkg>=1.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        pre_built=False,\n        parent_req=Requirement(\"foo\"),\n    )\n    assert result is None\n\n\ndef test_resolve_rejects_git_urls_for_source(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:\n    \"\"\"BootstrapRequirementResolver.resolve() rejects git URLs when pre_built=False.\"\"\"\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)\n\n    with pytest.raises(\n        ValueError, match=\"Git URL requirements must be handled by Bootstrapper\"\n    ):\n        resolver.resolve(\n            req=Requirement(\"package @ git+https://github.com/example/repo.git\"),\n            req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n            pre_built=False,\n            parent_req=None,\n        )\n\n\n@patch(\"fromager.resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider\")\ndef test_resolve_allows_git_urls_for_prebuilt(\n    mock_resolve: MagicMock,\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"BootstrapRequirementResolver.resolve() allows git URLs when pre_built=True (test mode fallback).\"\"\"\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)\n    req = Requirement(\"mypkg @ git+https://github.com/example/repo.git\")\n\n    # Call resolve with pre_built=None (should auto-detect)\n        results = resolver.resolve(\n            req=req,\n            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n            parent_req=None,\n            pre_built=None,\n        )\n\n        # Verify resolution was called\n        mock_resolve.assert_called_once()\n        assert len(results) == 1\n        url, version = results[0]\n        assert url == \"https://files.pythonhosted.org/mypackage-2.0.tar.gz\"\n        assert version == Version(\"2.0\")\n\n\ndef test_extend_known_versions_accumulates(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:\n    \"\"\"extend_known_versions() accumulates versions across calls.\"\"\"\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)\n    req1 = Requirement(\"mypkg>=1.0\")\n    req2 = Requirement(\"mypkg>=2.0\")\n\n    resolver.extend_known_versions(\n        req1,\n        pre_built=False,\n        result=[(\"https://files.test/mypkg-1.5.tar.gz\", Version(\"1.5\"))],\n    )\n    resolver.extend_known_versions(\n        req2,\n        pre_built=False,\n        result=[(\"https://files.test/mypkg-2.0.tar.gz\", Version(\"2.0\"))],\n    )\n\n    # Both versions are now available when filtering by the wider specifier\n    matching = resolver.get_matching_versions(req1, pre_built=False)\n    assert len(matching) == 2\n    assert matching[0][1] == Version(\"2.0\")\n    assert matching[1][1] == Version(\"1.5\")\n\n\ndef test_get_matching_versions_returns_independent_lists(\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"get_matching_versions() returns a new list each call.\"\"\"\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)\n    req = Requirement(\"mypkg>=1.0\")\n\n    resolver.extend_known_versions(\n        req,\n        pre_built=False,\n        result=[(\"https://files.test/mypkg-1.0.tar.gz\", Version(\"1.0\"))],\n    )\n    list1 = resolver.get_matching_versions(req, pre_built=False)\n    list2 = resolver.get_matching_versions(req, pre_built=False)\n\n    assert list1 == list2\n    assert list1 is not list2\n\n    # Mutating one does not affect the other\n    list1.append((\"https://files.test/bad.tar.gz\", Version(\"9.9\")))\n    list3 = resolver.get_matching_versions(req, pre_built=False)\n    assert len(list3) == 1\n\n\n@patch(\"fromager.resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider\")\ndef test_resolve_cache_returns_independent_lists(\n    mock_resolve: MagicMock,\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"resolve() returns independent list copies from the cache, not shared references.\"\"\"\n    req = Requirement(\"mypkg>=1.0\")\n    mock_resolve.return_value = [\n        (\"https://example.com/mypkg-2.0.tar.gz\", Version(\"2.0\")),\n        (\"https://example.com/mypkg-1.5.tar.gz\", Version(\"1.5\")),\n    ]\n\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)\n\n    # First call populates cache\n    results1 = resolver.resolve(\n        req=req,\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=False,\n        return_all_versions=True,\n    )\n\n    # Mutate the returned list\n    results1.append((\"https://example.com/injected.tar.gz\", Version(\"9.9\")))\n\n    # Second call should return clean cached data, unaffected by mutation\n    results2 = resolver.resolve(\n        req=req,\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=False,\n        return_all_versions=True,\n    )\n\n    assert len(results2) == 2\n    assert results1 is not results2\n    # Only called once — second call used cache\n    mock_resolve.assert_called_once()\n\n\n@patch(\"fromager.resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider\")\ndef test_toplevel_version_visible_to_transitive_via_cache(\n    mock_resolve: MagicMock,\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Version found via top-level bypass is visible to later transitive lookups.\n\n    Simulates the architect's scenario:\n    1. Top-level A==2.0.0 resolves with cooldown bypassed → v2.0 cached\n    2. Transitive A>=1.0 resolves with cooldown enforced → only v1.5 from network\n    3. But v2.0 is already in the package-level cache, so the transitive\n       lookup returns v2.0 as the highest matching version.\n    \"\"\"\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)\n\n    # Step 1: top-level resolves A==2.0.0 (cooldown bypassed)\n    mock_resolve.return_value = [\n        (\"https://files.test/mypkg-2.0.tar.gz\", Version(\"2.0\")),\n    ]\n    results_toplevel = resolver.resolve(\n        req=Requirement(\"mypkg==2.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=False,\n    )\n    assert results_toplevel[0][1] == Version(\"2.0\")\n    assert mock_resolve.call_count == 1\n\n    # Step 2: transitive resolves A>=1.0 (cooldown enforced, only finds v1.5)\n    mock_resolve.return_value = [\n        (\"https://files.test/mypkg-1.5.tar.gz\", Version(\"1.5\")),\n    ]\n    results_transitive = resolver.resolve(\n        req=Requirement(\"mypkg>=1.0\"),\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=False,\n    )\n    assert mock_resolve.call_count == 2\n\n    # The transitive lookup sees v2.0 from the package-level cache (found\n    # during top-level resolution) even though the transitive network call\n    # only returned v1.5.\n    assert results_transitive[0][1] == Version(\"2.0\")\n\n\n@patch(\"fromager.resolver.find_all_matching_from_provider\")\ndef test_resolve_prebuilt_after_source_uses_separate_cache(\n    mock_resolve: MagicMock,\n    tmp_context: WorkContext,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"resolve(pre_built=True) after same req resolved as source uses separate cache.\"\"\"\n    req = Requirement(\"testpkg==1.5\")\n\n    # Second call: wheel resolution\n        [\n            (\n                \"https://files.pythonhosted.org/testpkg-1.5-py3-none-any.whl\",\n                Version(\"1.5\"),\n            )\n        ],\n    ]\n\n    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context)\n\n    # First call: resolve as source (explicit pre_built=False)\n    results1 = resolver.resolve(\n        req=req,\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=False,\n    )\n\n    assert len(results1) == 1\n    url1, version1 = results1[0]\n    assert url1 == \"https://files.pythonhosted.org/testpkg-1.5.tar.gz\"\n    assert version1 == Version(\"1.5\")\n    assert mock_resolve.call_count == 1\n\n    # Second call: resolve same req as prebuilt (explicit pre_built=True)\n    # This should NOT return the cached source result\n    results2 = resolver.resolve(\n        req=req,\n        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n        parent_req=None,\n        pre_built=True,\n    )\n\n    # failure = ResolverException(\"no candidates match\")\n\n    # Act\n    with (\n        patch.object(resolver, \"_resolve_and_extend\", side_effect=failure),\n        pytest.raises(ResolverException) as exc_info,\n    ):\n        resolver.resolve(\n            req=Requirement(\"flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1\"),\n            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,\n            parent_req=Requirement(\"vllm\"),\n            pre_built=False,\n        )\n\n    # Assert\n    message = str(exc_info.value)\n    assert \"flashinfer-python==0.6.8.post1 required by vllm\" in message\n    assert \"no candidates match\" in message\n    assert exc_info.value.__cause__ is failure\n\n\nclass TestResolveFromCacheServer:\n    \"\"\"Tests for the cache server fallback in )\n        req = Requirement(\"testpkg\")\n\n        with patch(\n            \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.resolver\"\n            \".find_all_matching_from_provider\",\n            return_value=[\n                (\"http://cache.test/testpkg-3.0.whl\", Version(\"3.0\")),\n                (\"http://cache.test/testpkg-2.0.whl\", Version(\"2.0\")),\n            ],\n        ):\n            result = brr._resolve_from_cache_server(req)\n\n        assert len(result) == 1\n        assert result[0][1] == Version(\"3.0\")\n\n    def test_returns_empty_when_cache_has_no_match(\n        self, tmp_context: WorkContext\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Returns empty list when cache server has nothing.\"\"\"\n        brr = BootstrapRequirementResolver(\n            tmp_context,\n            multiple_versions=True,\n            cache_wheel_server_url=\"http://cache.test/simple\",\n        )\n        req = Requirement(\"testpkg\")\n\n        with patch(\n brr._resolve_from_cache_server(req)\n\n        assert result == []\n\n    def test_returns_empty_on_exception(self, tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:\n        \"\"\"Returns empty list when cache server query fails.\"\"\"\n        brr = BootstrapRequirementResolver(\n            tmp_context,\n            multiple_versions=True,\n            cache_wheel_server_url=\"http://cache.test/simple\",\n        )\n        req = Requirement(\"testpkg\")\n\n        with patch(\n            \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.resolver\"\n            \".find_all_matching_from_provider\",\n            side_effect=RuntimeError(\"connection refused\"),\n        ):\n            result = brr._resolve_from_cache_server(req)\n\n        assert result == []\n\n    def test_resolve_uses_cache_fallback_when_age_filter_empties(\n        self, tmp_context: WorkContext\n    ) -> None:\n        \"\"\"resolve() falls back to cache server when age filter           patch(\n                \"fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver.sources.get_source_provider\",\n            ),\n            patch(\n ):\n            result = brr.resolve(\n                req,\n                RequirementType.INSTALL,\n                parent_req=None,\n                pre_built=False,\n                return_all_versions=True,\n            )\n\n        mock_pypi.assert_called_once()\n        mock_cache.assert_called_once_with(req)\n        assert len(result) == 1\n        assert result[0][1] == """Tests for bootstrap_requirement_resolver module."""

from unittest.mock import MagicMock, patch

import pytest
from packaging.requirements import Requirement
from packaging.utils import canonicalize_name
from packaging.version import Version
from resolvelib.resolvers import ResolverException

from fromager.bootstrap_requirement_resolver import BootstrapRequirementResolver
from fromager.context import WorkContext
from fromager.dependency_graph import DependencyGraph
from fromager.requirements_file import RequirementType

# Test fixture: previous dependency graph
old_graph = DependencyGraph()

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("foo"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("foo"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
    req_version=Version("7"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("bar"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("bar"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
    req_version=Version("6"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=None,
    parent_version=None,
    req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
    req=Requirement("blah"),
    req_version=Version("1.0.0"),
)

old_graph.add_dependency(
    parent_name=canonicalize_name("blah"),
    parent_version=Version("1.0.0"),
    req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
    req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
    req_version=Version("5"),
)


def test_resolve_from_graph_no_changes(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver resolves from previous graph with no changes."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Resolving new dependency that doesn't exist in graph
    assert (
        resolver._resolve_from_graph(
            req=Requirement("xyz"),
            req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
            pre_built=False,
            parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
        )
        is None
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("7"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_upgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver prefers top-level requirements over history."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of pbr==8
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("pbr==8"),
        req_version=Version("8"),
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo - should get upgraded version from top-level
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("8"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar - constraint prevents upgrade
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_install_dep_downgrade(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver handles version downgrades from top-level requirements."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)

    # Simulating new bootstrap with a toplevel requirement of pbr<=6
    tmp_context.dependency_graph.add_dependency(
        parent_name=None,
        parent_version=None,
        req_type=RequirementType.TOP_LEVEL,
        req=Requirement("pbr<=6"),
        req_version=Version("6"),
    )

    # Resolving pbr dependency of foo - gets downgraded to 6
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("foo"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of bar - already at 6
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr>=5,<7"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("bar"),
    ) == [("", Version("6"))]

    # Resolving pbr dependency of blah - exact version requirement
    assert resolver._resolve_from_graph(
        req=Requirement("pbr==5"),
        req_type=RequirementType.INSTALL,
        pre_built=False,
        parent_req=Requirement("blah"),
    ) == [("", Version("5"))]


def test_resolve_from_graph_toplevel_dep(tmp_context: WorkContext) -> None:
    """BootstrapRequirementResolver resolves top-level dependencies correctly."""
    resolver = BootstrapRequirementResolver(tmp_context, old_graph)
